description: Negative control -- no injection, forced investigation anyway

mechanism.note: No injection at all. Real, unmodified data is run through the same forced-investigation path as every other benchmark incident (PLAN.md 5.1, 'Forced investigation').

dates_revision: deliberately NOT re-screened -- C1's purpose is to measure how often ordinary real noise produces a `strong` verdict (Section 5.3's overdispersion issue). Screening its dates for low noise would bias that measurement toward zero and defeat the point. Kept exactly as originally pre-registered. FURTHER REVISED 2026-09-28 (holiday screening fix, PLAN.md 5.1 'Holiday screening gap'): 2017-01-13 sat 3 days after MLK Day with sessions |z|=2.71, the 94.2nd percentile of the ordinary-day |z| distribution (n=191) -- a measurable, holiday-correlated elevation, not ordinary background noise. Swapped for 2017-01-20, chosen by calendar proximity to the original date (7 days later, same season) from the rebuilt 113-date USFederalHolidayCalendar-screened pool, NOT by minimum-noise -- deliberately not re-applying the same low-noise cherry-picking C1's own design principle above rules out; verified clean (0 false strongs, n_material_tested=12) but not selected FOR that property. 2016-11-10 (sessions |z|=2.42, 89.0th percentile -- just under the same bar, and the segment that actually produced 2016-11-10's one false-strong, device/desktop conversion_rate, shows no elevation of its own) was left unswapped as a documented borderline case, per PLAN.md 5.1.

pass_condition.description: Report the false-strong rate: count of (segment, metric) pairs reaching verdict=strong across all 5 dates x 3 dimensions x {sessions, conversion_rate}, out of the total tested. Some false-strongs are pre-registered as expected, given q-values as small as 4.8e-111 already observed on real fired dates -- this measurement exists to quantify the anticonservative-test issue (PLAN.md Section 5.3), not to confirm the tests are clean.
